questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which Rajput ruler defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain?

The First Battle of Tarain (also called the Battle of Taraori) was fought in 1191 AD near Tarain, close to present-day Haryana, between Prithviraj Chauhan (the ruler of Ajmer and Delhi) and Muhammad Ghori (the Ghurid ruler of Afghanistan). Ghori’s forces advanced into India, aiming to expand their empire. In this battle, Prithviraj Chauhan’s Rajput army defeated Ghori decisively, and Ghori himself was badly injured and forced to retreat. This victory highlighted the military strength of the Rajputs. However, Muhammad Ghori returned the very next year with a stronger and better-prepared army. In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD), Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, which became a turning point in Indian history as it laid the foundation for Muslim rule in North India.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which Indian space mission marked the successful launch of 104 satellites in a single mission?

On 15 February 2017, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) created a world record by successfully launching 104 satellites in a single mission from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. The main payload was Cartosat-2D, an earth observation satellite, along with 103 co-passenger satellites. Out of these, 96 satellites belonged to the USA, while the rest were from countries like Israel, Kazakhstan, Netherlands, Switzerland, UAE, and India. This mission demonstrated India’s ability to launch multiple satellites efficiently at low cost, making ISRO a global leader in space technology. It also showcased India’s growing role in the commercial space market, as many foreign nations relied on ISRO for launching their satellites. The success of PSLV-C37 further cemented ISRO’s reputation as a reliable and cost-effective space agency worldwide.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} In which year were the major economic reforms introduced in India?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is 1991. India faced a severe economic crisis in 1991, with foreign exchange reserves barely enough to cover a few weeks of imports. To tackle this, the Government of India under Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh introduced a series of major economic reforms. These reforms are known as the Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation (LPG) reforms. The reforms included measures like devaluation of the rupee, reduction in import tariffs, ending the Licence Raj, encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI), and liberalising industrial policies. This marked a turning point in India’s economy, shifting from a closed, centrally planned system to a market-oriented, globally integrated economy. These reforms not only stabilized India’s economic situation but also laid the foundation for rapid growth in the following decades, transforming India into one of the world’s fastest-growing economies.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The term "deuce" is associated with which sport?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Tennis. In tennis, the term "deuce" is used when both players have scored 40–40, meaning the score is tied at a crucial point. At deuce, a player must win two consecutive points to win the game – the first point gives "advantage," and if the player wins the next point, they win the game. However, if the opponent wins the next point after deuce, the score returns to deuce again. This rule makes tennis more competitive and ensures that a game cannot be won by a single point once it reaches 40–40. The concept of deuce highlights the endurance, mental strength, and consistency required in tennis.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which schedule of the Constitution contains provisions for the disqualification of legislators under the anti-defection law?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Tenth Schedule. The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, also known as the Anti-Defection Law, was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985. It provides the grounds on which legislators (both MPs and MLAs) can be disqualified on the basis of defection. A member is disqualified if they voluntarily give up the membership of the party, or if they vote/abstain against the direction of the party without prior permission. The power to decide disqualification lies with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha/State Legislative Assembly, depending on the case. This law was enacted to curb political instability caused by frequent defections and to strengthen democracy by ensuring party discipline.

questions.question:

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which of the following is not a correct statement regarding vacuoles?

options.A: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} In some plant cells, the central vacuole can take up most of the cell’s volume
options.B: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Vacuoles serve as storage sacs for both solids and liquids
options.C: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Vacuoles are generally larger in animal cells than in plant cells
options.D: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Animal cells usually contain smaller vacuoles compared to plant cells

questions.correct_answer: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Vacuoles are generally larger in animal cells than in plant cells
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is “Vacuoles are generally larger in animal cells than in plant cells.” This is incorrect because in reality, plant cells generally have a single large central vacuole that occupies up to 80–90% of the cell’s volume, playing a major role in maintaining turgor pressure, storing nutrients, and waste management. In contrast, animal cells contain multiple small vacuoles, which are much smaller in size and perform functions like storage and transport. Hence, vacuoles are larger in plant cells, not in animal cells.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Name the Indian port that is the largest exporter of iron ore?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Marmagao Port. It handles a large share of India’s total iron ore exports to countries like Japan, China, and South Korea. The port developed extensively during the 20th century due to Goa’s rich iron ore deposits and remains strategically vital for India’s mineral trade. Paradip Port (Odisha) mainly handles coal, crude oil, and fertilizers. Visakhapatnam Port (Andhra Pradesh) is important for coal and petroleum products. Chennai Port (Tamil Nadu) is known for automobiles and general cargo, not iron ore. Hence, Marmagao Port is the largest exporter of iron ore in India.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} A conductor rod moving with a velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. If the length of the rod perpendicular to both v and B is L, the induced EMF across its ends is given by?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is BLv. According to Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction, the induced EMF (ε) in a conductor moving in a magnetic field is given by: ε = B × L × v Here, B = magnetic field strength L = length of the conductor v = velocity of the conductor (perpendicular to both L and B) The derivation comes from the formula: ε = dΦ/dt = B × A/time, where the rate of change of magnetic flux (Φ) leads to induced EMF. Since the rod sweeps an area (A = L × displacement), and displacement/time = velocity, the formula reduces to ε = BLv. This principle is the working foundation of devices like electric generators, railguns, and electromagnetic brakes.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The Vice-President of India is part of which branch of the government?

As the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, he is an integral part of the Legislature. At the same time, being the second-highest constitutional office after the President, he is also a part of the Executive branch. In the absence of the President (due to death, resignation, removal, or otherwise), the Vice-President acts as the Acting President of India. Thus, the Vice-President connects both the Executive and Legislative wings of the Indian government.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which of the following is a subject under the State List?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Public Order. Under the Indian Constitution, subjects of governance are divided into three lists—Union List, State List, and Concurrent List—as given in the Seventh Schedule. Matters of national importance like defence, foreign affairs, and banking fall under the Union List. Subjects of both national and regional importance, like education, forests, and marriage laws, are in the Concurrent List, where both Centre and States can make laws. However, Public Order and Police are explicitly placed under the State List, meaning that only State Governments have the authority to legislate and administer them. This ensures that law and order, being a matter of local governance, is handled directly by the State.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which of the following is a key reason for the decline in the agricultural sector in India after 1991 economic reforms?

After the 1991 economic reforms, India adopted a policy of liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation. This led to an agricultural shift towards cash crops for export, such as cotton, sugarcane, and oilseeds, rather than traditional food crops. At the same time, the government reduced subsidies and public investment in key areas like irrigation, rural infrastructure, and agricultural research. These changes made farmers more vulnerable to international price fluctuations and reduced overall productivity growth in agriculture.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which scheme was launched to promote entrepreneurship among SC and ST communities?

Under this scheme, banks are required to provide loans between ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore to at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up a new enterprise. It aims to empower disadvantaged groups by facilitating their participation in economic activities and self-employment.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which force governs the motion of planets, stars, and galaxies?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Gravitational force. It is the weakest of the four fundamental forces, yet it is the most dominant at astronomical scales. Gravitational force governs the motion of planets around the Sun, stars in galaxies, and even the galaxies themselves. For example, Earth revolves around the Sun due to the Sun’s gravitational pull, and the Moon revolves around the Earth for the same reason. Without gravity, the large-scale structure of the universe would not exist.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility states that as a consumer consumes more and more units of a commodity:

questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Marginal utility derived from each additional unit decreases. The Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility in economics states that when a consumer keeps consuming additional units of the same good, the satisfaction (utility) gained from each extra unit decreases after a certain point. For example, eating one slice of pizza gives high satisfaction, the second gives slightly less, and by the fourth or fifth slice, the satisfaction may become very low or even negative.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.solution:
*{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya. He founded the Maurya Empire in 321 BCE after overthrowing the Nanda dynasty with the guidance and support of Chanakya (Kautilya), the author of Arthashastra. Chandragupta united most of the Indian subcontinent under one central administration, making it the first major empire in India. His reign laid the foundation for political unity and strong administration. Later, his grandson Ashoka the Great expanded the empire to its greatest territorial extent and spread Buddhism.

questions.question:

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which of the following is the specific port facility within Chabahar Port that India is primarily developing and operating?

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which principle of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ensures that entities collecting personal data must obtain explicit consent from individuals?

This ensures that individuals have control over their personal information and can make informed choices. It establishes transparency and accountability for data fiduciaries. Other principles like Purpose Limitation deal with restricting use of data to specific purposes, Data Localization relates to storing data within the country, and Storage Reduction Compliance concerns minimizing data retention. Hence, only Notice and Choice Framework ensures explicit consent from individuals.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which Mughal Emperor issued the Deccan campaign against the Marathas and spent significant time in the region? ?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Aurangzeb. Aurangzeb shifted his capital to the Deccan region and spent nearly 25 years (1681–1707) engaged in battles against the Marathas, Bijapur, and Golconda. These campaigns strained the Mughal treasury and weakened the empire. His continuous struggle with the Marathas, especially against leaders like Shivaji and later Sambhaji, turned the Deccan into the centre of Mughal-Maratha conflicts. questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} What is the scientific term for white blood cells?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Leucocytes. White blood cells (WBCs) are scientifically known as leucocytes. Their main function is to defend the body against infections, bacteria, viruses, and other foreign invaders. They form a crucial part of the immune system. There are several types of WBCs such as neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils, each with specialized roles in immunity. The term "Erythrocytes" refers to red blood cells (RBCs), which transport oxygen. "Thrombocytes" or platelets are responsible for blood clotting. Hence, the correct term for white blood cells is leucocytes.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which of the following is recognized as a classical dance of India?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Bharatnatyam. It is one of the eight officially recognized classical dance forms of India. Bharatnatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is deeply connected with devotional themes, especially dedicated to Lord Shiva. It combines expressive gestures (mudras), rhythmic movements, and storytelling to depict spiritual ideas from Hindu scriptures like the Natya Shastra. In contrast, Bhangra (Punjab), Lavani (Maharashtra), and Garba (Gujarat) are important folk dances but are not classified as classical dances. Bharatnatyam’s antiquity and codified traditions give it classical status.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which of these rivers does not originate in the Peninsular Plateau of India?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Ganga River. The Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas (Uttarakhand) and not from the Peninsular Plateau. In contrast, the Cauvery, Godavari, and Krishna rivers all originate from the Peninsular Plateau. Cauvery originates from the Western Ghats in Karnataka, Godavari from Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra, and Krishna from Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra. The Peninsular rivers are rain-fed and seasonal, while the Ganga is a Himalayan river that is perennial, fed by both rainfall and melting glaciers. Thus, the Ganga stands out as the only river among the options that does not belong to the Peninsular Plateau river system.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Under which article can the President declare a National Emergency?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Article 352. Article 352 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to proclaim a National Emergency if he/she is satisfied that the security of India or any part of its territory is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. Originally, the term used was “internal disturbance,” but the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) replaced it with “armed rebellion” to prevent misuse. Once proclaimed, the federal structure of India is significantly altered, as the Union government assumes greater power over the states. Fundamental Rights, particularly under Article 19, can remain suspended during the operation of a National Emergency. India has witnessed the proclamation of National Emergency thrice – in 1962 (China war), 1971 (Indo-Pak war), and 1975 (internal emergency declared by Indira Gandhi). Thus, Article 352 is the constitutional basis for National Emergencies, whereas Article 356 deals with President’s Rule in states, and Article 360 with Financial Emergency.

questions.question: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Which of the following rivers forms a delta along the Eastern Coastal Plains?
questions.solution: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The correct answer is Godavari River. The Godavari, also called the "Dakshin Ganga" or "Ganga of the South," is the largest river of peninsular India and flows eastwards into the Bay of Bengal. As it slows down near its mouth, it deposits huge amounts of alluvium, thereby forming an extensive delta in the Eastern Coastal Plains, particularly in Andhra Pradesh. In contrast, rivers like the Narmada, Tapi, and Mahi flow westwards into the Arabian Sea and form estuaries rather than deltas because of their narrow and submerged coastal plains. Deltas are typically formed by large rivers with broad floodplains, slow gradient near the mouth, and heavy silt load—conditions that the Godavari fulfills. The fertile Godavari delta is also famous for intensive agriculture, particularly rice cultivation, and supports dense settlements.

The Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920 was very limited in scope, allowing only the collection of simple physical measurements like fingerprints and footprints of convicts. In contrast, the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022 significantly expands the scope by authorising police and prison officials to collect a wide range of biometric and biological data, including iris scans, retina scans, facial recognition, DNA samples, behavioural attributes, and other modern identification techniques. This makes the 2022 Act more comprehensive and technology-driven, aligning with modern law enforcement requirements. This expansion has been justified on grounds of aiding investigation, improving conviction rates, and keeping pace with evolving crimes, though it has also raised debates regarding privacy and misuse of sensitive personal data.

Researchers in quantum computing face the twin difficulties of (1) _____ qubit coherence and (2) _____ error rates. While superconducting qubits have shown promise, maintaining coherence beyond microseconds remains (3) _____ due to environmental decoherence. Furthermore, scaling up the number of qubits requires (4) _____ control electronics that themselves introduce noise. To overcome these hurdles, teams are exploring (5) _____ techniques such as surface codes and topological qubits.

What should come in the place of blank 2?
questions.solution:
*{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Explanation
The passage discusses difficulties, so "prohibitive error rates"—meaning very high or unacceptable error rates—fits the context of challenges in quantum computing.

"Negligible," "cheap," and "low" suggest minimal or affordable error rates, which contradict the challenge described.

Identify the error in the sentence.
By the time they arrive, the concert had ended.
questions.solution:
*{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Explanation
The sentence mixes present tense ("arrive") with past perfect tense ("had ended"), which creates a tense inconsistency.

Since the action of arriving is expected to occur before the concert ended, "arrive" should be in the past tense to match the sequence of events. The corrected sentence is:

"By the time they arrived, the concert had ended."
Here, "had ended" (past perfect) shows the concert ended before they arrived (simple past).

questions.question:
*{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The following sentence is in indirect speech. Choose the option that conveys it in direct speech.
He said that he had been waiting there for more than two hours before the gates finally opened.

options.A: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} He said, I was waiting here for more than two hours before the gates finally opened.
options.B: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} He said, "I have been waiting here since two hours before the gates opened.”
options.C: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} He said, "I had waiting there before the gates opened.”
options.D: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} He said, I waited here two hours before gates opened.”

questions.correct_answer: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} He said, I was waiting here for more than two hours before the gates finally opened.
questions.solution:
*{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Explanation:
The indirect speech uses past perfect continuous ("had been waiting"), which typically changes to past continuous ("was waiting") in direct speech.

The reporting verb "said" is used with a comma before the quotation.

The pronouns change accordingly from third person indirect ("he") to first person direct ("I").

The time expressions remain similar to reflect the same meaning.

questions.question:
*{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The teacher who had conducted the workshop earlier, (1)/ along with his assistants, (2)/ have submitted the final report to the board (3)/ before the deadline last week. (4)

options.A: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} along with his assistants (2)
options.B: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} before the deadline last week (4)
options.C: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} have submitted the final report to the board (3)
options.D: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} The teacher who had conducted the workshop earlier {1)

questions.correct_answer: *{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} have submitted the final report to the board (3)
questions.solution:
*{overflow-wrap: break-word;} img {max-width:100% !important} Explanation
The subject "The teacher" is singular.

The phrase "along with his assistants" is a parenthetical and does not change the number of the subject.

Therefore, the verb must be singular to agree with the singular subject.

"Have submitted" is plural; the correct verb form should be "has submitted."
